claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCrAl powder has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Non-preheated 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces a bond coat with inadequate thickness.
The feedstock should be preheated to approximately 200–300 °C immediately before torch injection.
Moderate feedstock preheating increases particle surface temperature and plasticity.
The increased plasticity improves particle deformation and splat formation upon impact.
Improved splat formation produces better intersplat bonding.
Preheating improves the particles' viscosity and malleability at impact.
Improved flattening and cohesion between successive splats increase deposition efficiency and coating build-up.
A controlled preheat temperature combined with an inert atmosphere avoids additional oxidation.
Preheating is expected to produce a significantly thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than the non-preheated baseline.
The preheated process may produce a bond-coat thickness approaching or exceeding 100 μm.
The thicker coating will retain microstructural integrity.
The preheated process will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Excessive feedstock heating may increase oxidation risk.
Excessive feedstock heating may adversely alter powder morphology.
The intervention should remain effective under typical thermal-spray processing and service conditions that do not accelerate oxidation kinetics.
The optimal preheat temperature and quantitative thickness improvement require experimental calibration.

contradictions.description: The 15–45 μm value is initially identified as the feedstock particle-size range, but other fields treat it as the baseline deposit or bond-coat thickness. Thus the baseline coating thickness is conflated with the powder size distribution.
